title: Find Minimum Element
statement: Find the smallest element in an array.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the selects maximum instead of minimum behavior in findMin; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch array indices / comparisons / loop boundaries / return values at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of findMin: Initialize minimum to the first actual array element and compare all remaining elements.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `if (arr[i] > best) best = arr[i];`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in selects maximum instead of minimum, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Initialize minimum to the first actual array element and compare all remaining elements.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `if (arr[i] > best) best = arr[i];` with `if (arr[i] < best) best = arr[i];` in findMin, then retest T1–T6.
